summary: Your own party overrides you: {the body}, where your own party holds the majority, overrides your veto of {the bill}, and {chamber leader} tells the press the votes were never in doubt.
realLife: One life: As South Carolina governor, his own party's House overrode 105 of his 106 budget vetoes in one day in 2004. The next day he brought live pigs into the chamber to protest pork spending. In 2006 he rejected the whole budget, and the legislature overrode him the next day. Another: In 2013, his first year as Indiana governor, the Republican legislature overrode his veto of a local tax bill by wide margins in both houses.

branches.then: The picture runs everywhere. Voters like it, and the senior members whose projects you mocked remember it at the next vote.
The body overrides you the next day in a special sitting, and the press calls it a failed protest.
The override is your first break with the majority, and members learn that your veto can be beaten.
